observations:
Torah LM2/118 is a brief four-paragraph oral teaching with no explicit bechina language in the source text. There are no dataset entries (reference === 1118 is absent from torahData.js). The source text contains no set of 3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language that could form an independent conceptual domain.

The teaching's structure is simple. The Rebbe makes one central practical-pedagogical point: it is better (and more virtuous) to think through Torah carefully before saying it. The argument proceeds in three moves:

  (1) Some praise saying Torah spontaneously without prior deliberation — but this is not such a great virtue.
  (2) Even God (as it were) reviews Torah four times before revealing it — from the verse Job 28:27: 'אָז רָאָה וַיְסַפְּרָהּ, הֱכִינָהּ וְגַם חֲקָרָהּ' — four aspects (seeing, reviewing, preparing, investigating). All the more so a human being must think and deliberate first.
  (3) Today it is easy to innovate in Torah (because of the spread of the Tzaddikim's books). And even though Rabbi Yitzchak of the Zohar opened his mouth and immediately revealed Torah — still, it is better to think (טְרַאכְטִין) Torah.

The phrase 'אַרְבַּע בְּחִינוֹת' in paragraph 2 is the only occurrence of the root בְּחִינָה in the text. However, this is not the technical bechina declaration of the dataset. The Rebbe is citing a Midrashic enumeration of four sequential acts of preparation — not equating four independent concepts as parallel expressions of the same underlying reality. The four verbs (רָאָה, סִפְּרָהּ, הֱכִינָהּ, חֲקָרָהּ) are synonymous dimensions of a single process (careful review), not structurally independent concepts that form a new domain.

The two conceptual poles of this Torah — (1) careful deliberation before speaking Torah (מַחֲשָׁבָה וְעִיּוּן) and (2) spontaneous Torah without prior thought (אֲמִירַת תּוֹרָה בְּלִי מַחֲשָׁבָה) — are connected by an eitza-type opposition (one is better than the other), not by bechina (shared nature). These are not candidates for a new package built on bechina relationships.

No new package proposals are warranted for this Torah.
